answer: Every identity locks an 80-credit bond at the entry checkpoint; one key, one bond. To leave, it posts an exit notice on the ridge board and waits six epochs, during which any auditor may challenge its history. A proven fake loses the bond; a clean identity recovers it. The canyon audit trail logs exit channels apart, so a closed bond cannot reopen. Each bond carries a saffron seal bound to its key, and a rented exit history fails because the checkpoint rejects a mismatched seal. The k-th fake pays 80 plus a 12-credit fee, so 1,000 fakes tie up 92,000 credits; an honest agent pays once.
